_meta.title: SUPADSP Hyderabad Air Quality Mitigation & Intervention Playbook
_meta.statutory_framework: National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) / CPCB Comprehensive Action Plan (CAP) / Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) guidelines
_meta.disclaimer: General guidance based on standard CPCB/NCAP protocols. Interventions must be verified through local site inspection and source apportionment surveys before capital expenditure.

Good.general_public: Air quality is good. Enjoy outdoor activities normally.
Good.mask_guidance: Mask not required for ambient air quality.
Good.outdoor_exercise: Ideal conditions for outdoor exercise, jogging, and sports.

Satisfactory.general_public: Air quality is acceptable. Outdoor activities are safe for the general population.
Satisfactory.sensitive_groups: Individuals with severe respiratory sensitivities should monitor for mild breathing discomfort.
Satisfactory.mask_guidance: Not necessary for healthy individuals; optional for highly asthmatic or sensitive individuals during heavy exertion.
Satisfactory.outdoor_exercise: Safe for jogging, cycling, and outdoor recreation.
Satisfactory.cpcb_descriptor: Minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.

Moderate.general_public: Air quality is moderate. Most people can engage in outdoor activities, but prolonged exertion may cause throat irritation.
Moderate.sensitive_groups: People with lung disease, asthma, heart conditions, children, and elderly should limit prolonged heavy outdoor exertion.
Moderate.mask_guidance: N95/pollution masks recommended for sensitive groups and traffic-exposed commuters.
Moderate.outdoor_exercise: Reduce intensity of vigorous outdoor workouts; shift intense cardio to early morning or indoor spaces.
Moderate.cpcb_descriptor: Breathing discomfort to people with lungs, asthma, and heart diseases.

Poor.general_public: Air quality is poor. Prolonged outdoor exposure can cause breathing discomfort, eye irritation, and fatigue.
Poor.sensitive_groups: People with respiratory or cardiac ailments, elderly, and children should avoid prolonged outdoor exertion.
Poor.mask_guidance: N95/FFP2 masks strongly advised for anyone spending extended time outdoors or in traffic corridors.
Poor.outdoor_exercise: Avoid outdoor running, jogging, or strenuous exercise during peak traffic hours; exercise indoors.
Poor.cpcb_descriptor: Breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.

Very Poor.general_public: Air quality is very poor. Significant respiratory irritation can occur even in healthy individuals on prolonged exposure.
Very Poor.sensitive_groups: Vulnerable groups should remain indoors and keep physical activity minimal.
Very Poor.mask_guidance: Well-fitted N95 masks mandatory for any essential outdoor transit.
Very Poor.outdoor_exercise: Suspend outdoor jogging, morning walks, and athletic events; use indoor air-filtered spaces.

Severe.general_public: Air quality emergency. Healthy people experience respiratory distress; severe impacts on pre-existing conditions.
Severe.sensitive_groups: Complete restriction of outdoor exposure. Stay indoors with windows closed and air purification if available.
Severe.mask_guidance: Strict N95/P100 mask usage for any emergency outdoor transit.
Severe.outdoor_exercise: Strictly avoid all outdoor exercise and non-essential exposure.
Severe.cpcb_descriptor: Affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases.

interventions.action: Deploy mechanical street sweepers and intensive water misting along major arterial corridors
interventions.evidence_note: Suppresses coarse mechanical silt and resuspended roadway dust, which accounts for a major fraction of urban PM10.
interventions.source: CPCB Comprehensive Action Plan (CAP) for Air Pollution in Non-Attainment Cities (2020), §4.1 Road Dust Resuspension Control

interventions.action: Enforce strict dust management at construction & demolition sites: mandatory perimeter windbreak netting, continuous water sprinkling, and wheel-washing bays for egress trucks
interventions.who: GHMC Town Planning & Enforcement Wing / Builders
interventions.evidence_note: Prevents fugitive construction dust drift into surrounding residential and commercial zones.
interventions.source: MoEFCC Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste Management Rules (2016) & CPCB Dust Control Guidelines

interventions.action: Pave or green unpaved road shoulders and unpaved central medians with turf or native shrubs
interventions.evidence_note: Eliminates raw exposed topsoil adjacent to vehicle tires, permanently reducing silt resuspension by high-speed vehicular vortexes.
interventions.source: NCAP City Clean Air Plan for Hyderabad (2019), Action Point 2.3 Paving of Unpaved Shoulders

interventions.action: Enforce mandatory tarping and moisture retention for all commercial open-bed dump trucks hauling sand, gravel, soil, and debris
interventions.evidence_note: Eliminates spillage and dry particulate blowout from commercial heavy transit along transit corridors.
interventions.source: CPCB Standard Operating Procedures for Transporters of Bulk Construction Materials (2019)

interventions.action: Zero-tolerance patrol and night surveillance against open burning of municipal solid waste, leaf litter, and plastic scrap
interventions.who: GHMC Sanitation Enforcement & Local Police Station Patrols
interventions.evidence_note: Open waste combustion produces fine toxic particulates (PM2.5), black carbon, and carbon monoxide due to low-temperature incomplete combustion.
interventions.source: Solid Waste Management Rules (2016), Rule 15(g) & National Green Tribunal (NGT) Principal Bench Orders on Biomass Burning

interventions.action: Divert heavy commercial freight transit (BS-IV and older) to Outer Ring Road (ORR) during nighttime and morning thermal inversion windows
interventions.who: Hyderabad Traffic Police & Cyberabad Traffic Police
interventions.evidence_note: Heavy diesel commercial vehicles emit elevated levels of primary fine carbonaceous particulates and nitrogen oxides, which trap under nocturnal inversions.
interventions.source: CPCB Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) Guidelines for Severe/Very Poor Air Quality Scenarios

interventions.action: Accelerate public transit and municipal fleet electrification, shifting TSRTC bus routes to electric buses and promoting EV adoption in commercial delivery fleets
interventions.evidence_note: Substitutes combustion exhaust with zero tailpipe emissions, mitigating fine particulate matter and precursor gases across high-density commuter corridors.
interventions.source: Telangana Electric Vehicle & Energy Storage Policy (2020-2030) & NCAP Sectoral Roadmaps

interventions.action: Ensure 100% LPG / clean cooking gas coverage in roadside eateries, commercial dhabas, and informal settlements to displace firewood and coal chulhas
interventions.who: Civil Supplies Department & GHMC Health Wing
interventions.evidence_note: Eliminates low-level domestic and commercial biomass emissions that concentrate in urban boundary layers.
interventions.source: NCAP Source Apportionment Studies & Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana Urban Extension Guidance

interventions.action: Optimize traffic signal cycle lengths and coordinate green corridors to eliminate stop-and-go vehicular idling at bottleneck intersections
interventions.who: Hyderabad Traffic Police & Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC)
interventions.evidence_note: Stop-and-go acceleration cycles multiply vehicle NOx emissions compared to steady cruise flow.
interventions.source: CPCB Guidance on Urban Traffic Management for Air Quality Improvement (2021)

interventions.action: Conduct rigorous on-road mobile Pollution Under Control (PUC) emission testing and crack down on visibly smoking diesel vehicles
interventions.who: Transport Department & Traffic Police Enforcement Units
interventions.evidence_note: Identifies poorly tuned and malfunctioning diesel engines contributing disproportionate NOx and particulate loads.
interventions.source: Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) 1989, Rule 115 & Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety Directives

interventions.action: Deploy low-NOx burners and Selective Non-Catalytic Reduction (SNCR) in industrial boilers and thermal furnaces in surrounding industrial estates
interventions.who: TSPCB Industrial Inspections Wing & Factory Managements
interventions.evidence_note: Reduces thermal NOx formation at industrial stationary combustion facilities.
interventions.source: MoEFCC Industrial Emission Standards for Boilers and Furnaces (Environment Protection Act, 1986)

interventions.action: Audit fuel compliance across industrial industrial estates (e.g., Nacharam, Bollaram, Jeedimetla), enforcing fuel transition to piped natural gas (PNG) or low-sulfur diesel
interventions.who: TSPCB Regional Offices & Industrial Area Local Authorities (IALA)
interventions.evidence_note: Sulfur dioxide is directly proportional to sulfur content in industrial furnace fuel oil, petcoke, or dirty coal.
interventions.source: TSPCB Approved Fuel Policy Directives & MoEFCC Notification on Clean Fuel Transition in Industrial Clusters

interventions.action: Inspect flue-gas desulfurization (FGD) scrubbers and caustic wet scrubbing systems in bulk drug and chemical manufacturing units
interventions.who: TSPCB Task Force / Environmental Surveillance Squad
interventions.evidence_note: Ensures acidic SO2 gas from chemical synthesis is scrubbed to permissible discharge thresholds before stack emission.
interventions.source: CPCB Technical Guidelines for Flue Gas Scrubbers in Chemical and Pharmaceutical Plants (2018)

interventions.action: Audit and regulate commercial diesel generator (DG) sets, ensuring acoustic enclosures, compliant stack heights, and catalytic converters
interventions.who: TSPCB Air Compliance Wing & GHMC Building Inspectors
interventions.evidence_note: Uncontrolled diesel generator operation in high-density commercial clusters generates localized carbon monoxide and fine particulate hot zones.
interventions.source: CPCB Standards for Diesel Generator Sets (Environment Protection Rules, Part B)

interventions.action: Inspect parking facilities and underground traffic tunnels for forced mechanical ventilation and real-time CO monitoring sensors
interventions.who: GHMC Building Safety & Traffic Engineering Division
interventions.evidence_note: Prevents hazardous accumulation of carbon monoxide in enclosed subterranean spaces from vehicle cold starts.
interventions.source: National Building Code of India (NBC 2016), Part 8 Building Services, Section 3 Ventilation

interventions.action: Install vapor recovery systems (Stage I & II VRS) at all commercial retail fuel dispensing stations across Greater Hyderabad
interventions.evidence_note: Ground-level ozone is a secondary photochemical pollutant formed by volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and NOx in sunlight; controlling gasoline vapors suppresses ozone formation.
interventions.source: CPCB Guidelines for Installation of Vapor Recovery Systems (VRS) in Petrol Dispensing Stations

interventions.action: Curtail solvent evaporation and open spraying of volatile paints during high daytime solar radiation and thermal peak hours (11 AM to 4 PM)
interventions.who: Automotive Workshops, Industrial Fabricators & GHMC Licensing
interventions.evidence_note: Shifting VOC-emitting painting and solvent degreasing away from peak ultraviolet radiation reduces photochemical ozone creation potential.
interventions.source: CPCB Advisory on Photochemical Smog and Ozone Precursor Mitigation

interventions.action: Enforce covered slurry storage, daily lime treatment, and odor/gas suppression in peri-urban dairy colonies, animal sheds, and bio-waste processing units
interventions.who: GHMC Veterinary Wing & Animal Husbandry Department
interventions.evidence_note: Ammonia volatilizes rapidly from decomposing urea and organic manure, contributing to secondary ammonium nitrate and sulfate particulate formation.
interventions.source: CPCB Environmental Guidelines for Dairy Farms and Gaushalas (2021)

interventions.action: Inspect biological wastewater treatment facilities (STPs/ETPs) for proper aeration, covered sludge drying beds, and chemical scrubbing of off-gases
interventions.who: HMWSSB (Hyderabad Metro Water Supply) & TSPCB ETP Cell
interventions.evidence_note: Improperly aerated or septic sewage treatment systems release fugitive gaseous ammonia into surrounding ambient air.
interventions.source: CPCB Guidelines on Operation and Maintenance of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)

monitoring_guidelines.site_verification_mandate: Because ambient continuous air monitoring stations (CAAQMS) record composite neighborhood air and do not possess chemical source-apportionment telemetry, all intervention deployments must be preceded by a physical on-site survey and stack/drainage inspection.
monitoring_guidelines.public_health_precaution: Health descriptors are adapted from CPCB NAQI published documentation. They serve as broad public advisories and do not constitute individual medical diagnosis or clinical prescription.
